faq.a: Richael (dh8116) is a Year 11 student in Auckland, New Zealand, who writes GPU kernels in Triton, fine-tunes and serves language models, and builds two AI products: Soulor AI and VNportal. Richael publishes a weekly Triton kernel benchmarked against PyTorch and leads a five-person research paper on verifier error in RLVR.

Soulor AI is an AI companion app with persistent memory and five relationship stages, from Stranger to Soulmate, plus a Simulation Mode that gives a panel of five AI perspectives on any situation. You can switch between the companion and the panel mid-conversation and the context carries over. Richael built it; it is in early access and free to start.

VNportal is a browser-based vinyl and music platform: find a record in the MusicBrainz database, play it, mix it on two decks, and create with AI music tools — no install, no hardware, no Spotify Premium. It also charts a rhythm game from a track's detected beats and generates single instruments locked to a tempo. Richael built it; it is in early access.

faq.q: What GPU kernels has Richael written?
faq.a: One Triton kernel a week, each benchmarked against PyTorch and published on this site with its numbers: vector add, fused softmax, flash attention, matmul, RMSNorm, RoPE, cross-entropy, fused linear + cross-entropy, and a fused SwiGLU MLP. The best result so far is fused cross-entropy at 15.90 ms against PyTorch's 24.03 ms at vocabulary size 131,072 (1.51x), with 1.67x less peak memory.

faq.q: What research is Richael working on?
faq.a: Richael leads a five-person paper on reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR): when does a verifier that is persistently wrong actually harm GRPO training? The study holds error rate and asymmetry fixed and sweeps persistence, and targets COLM or TMLR.

faq.q: What competitions has Richael placed in?
faq.a: Honorable Mention at HiMCM and in the IMMC regional round, AIME 10/15, AMC 12 Honor Roll (top 5%), and High Distinction in the Australian Mathematics Competition.
